winnerName: Seneca SC → Whitewater Falls → US-64 Cullasaja Gorge waterfall corridor → Bryson City & the Road to Nowhere → NC-28 Hellbender along Fontana/Cheoah Lakes → Fontana Dam → Cherohala Skyway westbound → Bald River Falls → Foothills Parkway (Look Rock) → Maryville/Alcoa TN
terminus: Maryville/Alcoa, TN — Home2 Suites by Hilton Alcoa Knoxville Airport (1864 Pauling St, Springbrook Farm; opened ~2023, free surface lot, ~$140-180); backup: Fairfield Inn & Suites Knoxville Airport Alcoa (1865 Pauling St, opened Aug 2020, ~$130-165), 100 yards away
routeSummary: Depart Seneca ~9:15am. (1) SC-130/NC-281 sweeper climb to Upper Whitewater Falls, 411 ft, 0.2-mi paved path (35.0296, -83.0159) — arrive ~10:10, 15-min stop. (2) US-64 Waterfall Byway: Bridal Veil Falls drive-up (35.0757, -83.2325) and walk-BEHIND Dry Falls (35.0681, -83.2387) ~11:15-11:45, beating the midday lot crush; Cullasaja Falls pull-off only if clear. (3) Franklin → Bryson City via US-441/74; fuel + quick lunch ~12:45-1:30 (last real services). (4) Road to Nowhere: 6.5-mi freshly repaved (2024-25) dead-end into the national park ending at the abandoned tunnel over Fontana Lake (~35.461, -83.538), out-and-back ~1:30-2:30 — the day's signature nobody-there stop. (5) NC-28 Hellbender sweepers along Fontana Lake with the Cable Cove Boat Ramp spur (~35.436, -83.765; short smooth gravel, sedan-safe) — the deserted-dock encore — then Fontana Dam (35.4518, -83.8046), ~2:30-3:45. (6) Cheoah Lake pull-offs + 2-min Fugitive dam peek (35.4519, -83.9385) ~4:00. (7) NC-143 → Cherohala Skyway westbound, 43 mi of flawless mile-high sweepers, Santeetlah Overlook 5,390 ft, ~4:15-5:45 (check radar at Robbinsville; run it stop-free if storms build). (8) Optional +30 min: Bald River Falls, a 90-ft waterfall viewed from the car on a paved bridge (35.3208, -84.1740; road rebuilt May 2025), ~6:00. (9) TN-360/72/US-129 along Chilhowee Lake → Foothills Parkway classic section, Look Rock Overlook (35.6338, -83.9418) ~7:00-7:30. (10) US-321 → Alcoa; arrive Home2 Suites ~7:45-8:15pm with 30-60 min of daylight left (sunset ~8:50pm). ~8.8-9.3h wheel time at realistic mountain pace, ~10.5-11h door-to-door.
reasoning: Seclusion (weighted highest) is where this corridor wins outright: the Road to Nowhere is the platonic ideal of the driver's stated #1 joy — turn off the main road, glass-smooth fresh pavement, dead-end at an abandoned tunnel over a lake, famously empty — and Cable Cove's lonely boat ramp is a near-literal replay of yesterday's Lake Hartwell dock highlight. Add empty Cheoah Lake pull-offs, a dozen deserted mile-high Cherohala overlooks, and a near-empty Look Rock, and it matches or beats every rival on nobody-there moments per hour. Scenery density is top-tier: five waterfalls (411-ft Whitewater, walk-behind Dry Falls, drive-up Bridal Veil, Cullasaja, drive-up 90-ft Bald River) plus two lakes, two dams, and 360° Smokies panoramas — all within the no-hike rule. Road fun for a 4,400-lb 7 Series is arguably the best of the four because it takes the Cherohala's wide third-gear sweepers and the Hellbender's lake sweepers while structurally SKIPPING the Dragon's miserable 2nd-gear hairpins that Candidates 2 and 3 force on the car. Crowd exposure is the lowest of the four on a post-holiday Monday (only Dry Falls midday and Deals Gap bike spillover; Gatlinburg never within 25 miles; Cades Cove deliberately skipped). Hotel fit is clean: a ~2023 Home2 at $140-180 with a free flat surface lot, plus a 2020 Fairfield backup next door — no Beckley-grade compromise on town charm, no Wytheville-grade compromise on building age. Most decisively, it is the only corridor that honestly fits the day: 8.8h driving → ~10.5-11h elapsed with a daylight arrival, versus 11.5-12h dark arrivals for Candidates 1 and 3. It also already functions as the best possible merge — it contains Candidate 2's crown jewels (Cherohala, Bald River Falls, Foothills/Look Rock) with a far better opening act and terminus; I verified that grafting Candidate 3's Burke's Garden finale is geometrically impossible (4+ h of backtracking from Fontana country to Tazewell VA), and swapping in Candidate 2's Corbin terminus adds ~1h40 of I-75 for marginal hotel gain while deleting the Foothills Parkway finale.
runnerUp: Candidate 3 (Blue Ridge Escarpment → Grayson Highlands → Back of the Dragon → Burke's Garden → Wytheville VA). It has the single best individual seclusion moment of any route — golden hour alone on the VA-623 crest above Burke's Garden — and its entire Virginia second half is emptier than anything on the winner. It loses because it is dishonest about time (~11.5-12h door-to-door, 9:00-9:45pm arrival with no dinner options), its marquee wildlife promise (Grayson ponies) needs a 1-2 mile walk that violates the no-hike rule, its tightest Clinch Mountain hairpins are first-gear labor in a long-wheelbase 7 Series, and Wytheville has no true new-build hotel (best is a 2019 Tru). If the driver ever gets a day with a 12-hour budget and lower hotel standards, run this one.
trimAdvice: The route needs no amputation to fit daylight, but three pre-planned levers exist if storms or fatigue hit: (1) drop the optional Foothills Parkway Wears Valley out-and-back entirely — it was already marked skippable (-50 min) and the classic Look Rock section delivers 90% of the view; (2) if afternoon radar looks ugly at Robbinsville (~4pm, the 2-5pm storm window), run the Cherohala without overlook stops and convert Bald River Falls into the day's final waterfall stop instead (-20 min net); (3) if running late out of the waterfall corridor, skip the Cullasaja Falls pull-off (tight shoulder, riskiest parking of the day for a 7 Series) and the Fontana Dam walk-across, keeping only the visitor-center viewpoint (-25 min). Do NOT cut the Road to Nowhere or Cable Cove — they are the profile's core payload. Firm rules regardless: fuel up in Franklin or Bryson City (no gas past Stecoah until Tellico Plains), download offline maps for the Fontana/Cherohala cell desert, check DriveNC.gov for US-64 Cullasaja Gorge one-lane signals and fs.usda.gov for Cherohala status the morning of, and hit Dry Falls before ~11:45am while the small lot is still post-holiday quiet.
